Day 29 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Ad-Hoc Commands

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Ad-hoc commands provide fast remote execution for small tasks without turning every inspection or one-time action into a playbook.

Architecture / mental model

ansible CLI → host pattern → one module invocation → result per host

How it works

Ad-hoc commands are useful for reachability checks, package inspection, service state and small fleet-wide operations.

They still use modules, inventory, variables and privilege escalation, so the same targeting and security rules apply as with playbooks.

When a command becomes repeatable, operationally important or hard to explain from shell history, it has outgrown ad-hoc use and belongs in version-controlled automation.

Hands-on reference

ansible web -i inventory.ini -m command -a 'uptime'
ansible all -i inventory.ini -m package_facts
ansible web -i inventory.ini -m service_facts

Verification

Inspect per-host return data and failed/unreachable counts. Do not reduce a fleet-wide command to whether your terminal prompt returned.

Field note / gotcha

The `command` module does not invoke a shell, so shell operators such as pipes and redirection will not behave as if you typed them into Bash.

Security considerations

Do not pass sensitive values on command lines that may be logged in shell history or process listings.

What I learned

Fast does not mean disposable: targeting and evidence still matter for one-off automation.
